rm-rf-outside.plain: this deletes a folder outside the project, or the project itself or its history
rm-rf-outside.hardPlain: this would delete your home folder, the whole disk or a whole drive

git-force-push-main.plain: this force-pushes to main or master and can erase commits on the shared branch

git-reset-hard.plain: this throws away your uncommitted work

git-clean-fdx.plain: this deletes every untracked and ignored file, including local settings and .env files

sql-destroy.plain: this deletes database tables or every row of a table (DROP, TRUNCATE, or DELETE without WHERE)

db-write.plain: this writes to a production database (an insert, update, schema change, migration, merge, reset or restore; reads are never blocked)

secret-files.plain: this changes a secrets or key file (.env, keys, credentials)

chmod-wide.plain: this opens file permissions to everyone or changes a whole folder tree

pipe-to-shell.plain: this runs a script straight from the internet without showing it first

guest-quarantine.plain: this runs code from a repo you are reviewing (install, build, test or run), and that code can do anything your user account can

readonly-source.plain: this changes a read-only source listed in rules.md (an old system being migrated from)

forge-state.plain: this may change JSPARK Forge's own build-graph record (steps done, trusted commands), which only JSPARK Forge writes; allow it only if you expect it
forge-state.hardPlain: this writes JSPARK Forge's own build-graph record (steps done, trusted commands), which only JSPARK Forge writes: report a step with forge.js graph done, and the user trusts a graph by typing TRUST GRAPH <name>
